items.q: Look at those dark clouds over the school gate! It ______ very soon.
items.vi: Nhìn mấy đám mây đen trên cổng trường kìa! Trời sắp mưa rồi.
items.explanation: A prediction from present evidence (Look at those dark clouds) takes be going to: is going to rain. ✗ rains — present simple is for habits or timetables, not a prediction; ✗ has rained — present perfect is a past action with a present result, but very soon points to the future; ✗ rained — past simple, but the rain has not happened yet.

items.q: Nam paid the taxi ______ with the coins he had left in his pocket.
items.vi: Nam trả tiền taxi bằng mấy đồng xu còn lại trong túi.
items.explanation: Money paid for a journey by taxi, bus or train is a fare (clue: paid the taxi). ✗ fee — money for a professional service or a course, not for a ride; ✗ fine — money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule; ✗ tip — extra money given as thanks, not the price of the trip itself.

items.q: There was ______ rain all afternoon, so the football match was cancelled.
items.vi: Mưa to suốt cả buổi chiều nên trận bóng đá đã bị hủy.
items.explanation: Rain in large amounts is heavy rain — the adjective that collocates with rain to mean 'a lot' (clue: the match was cancelled). ✗ strong — goes with wind or current, not rain; ✗ hard — works as an adverb (it rained hard) but 'hard rain' is not the standard noun phrase; ✗ big — describes the size of objects, never rain.

items.q: Lan: Did you buy the new maths workbook? / Nam: Yes, but I had to ______ for it at the shop near school.
items.vi: Lan: Cậu mua cuốn bài tập toán mới chưa? / Nam: Rồi, nhưng tớ phải trả giá cắt cổ ở tiệm gần trường.
items.explanation: Pay through the nose = pay far too much (but I had to signals a complaint about the price). ✗ pay lip service — support something only in words, and it takes 'to', not 'for'; ✗ pay my way — pay my own costs, nothing about an overpriced item; ✗ pay my respects — greet or honour someone politely, not buy a book.

items.q: Lan: Who ______ your little brother when your parents are at work? / Nam: My grandmother does.
items.vi: Lan: Ai trông em trai cậu khi bố mẹ cậu đi làm? / Nam: Bà tớ.
items.explanation: Look after = take care of someone; the reply My grandmother does (while the parents are at work) shows childcare. ✗ looks up — find information in a book or online; ✗ looks into — investigate a problem; ✗ looks for — search for something or someone lost.

items.q: Nam ______ have taken my umbrella — he wasn't even at school today.
items.vi: Nam không thể nào lấy ô của tớ được — hôm nay cậu ấy thậm chí còn không đi học.
items.explanation: Can't have + past participle = it was impossible in the past; the clue he wasn't even at school today proves it. ✗ must — must have means 'I am sure he did it', the opposite of the evidence; ✗ should — should have means he was expected to do it but didn't (advice or regret), not impossibility; ✗ needn't — needn't have means he did it but it was unnecessary.

items.q: The teacher ______ class we have on Monday mornings is going to retire next year.
items.vi: Cô giáo mà chúng tôi có tiết học vào các sáng thứ Hai sẽ nghỉ hưu vào năm sau.
items.explanation: A noun (class) follows the blank, so the relative pronoun must show possession: whose (= the teacher's class). ✗ who — a subject pronoun, must be followed by a verb, not a noun; ✗ which — used for things, and it cannot show possession; ✗ whom — an object pronoun for people, cannot show possession either.

items.q: Lan: Do you want to play badminton? / Nam: Sorry, I have too ______ homework to finish before nine.
items.vi: Lan: Cậu có muốn chơi cầu lông không? / Nam: Xin lỗi, tớ có quá nhiều bài tập về nhà phải làm xong trước chín giờ.
items.explanation: Homework is uncountable, so 'too + quantity' is too much. ✗ many — only with plural countable nouns (too many books); ✗ few — countable, and it means 'not enough', the wrong meaning; ✗ a lot — cannot follow too (you say 'a lot of homework' but never 'too a lot').

items.q: Remember ______ your project to school tomorrow — the teacher is going to collect it.
items.vi: Nhớ mang dự án đến trường ngày mai nhé — cô giáo sẽ thu đấy.
items.explanation: Remember + to-infinitive = don't forget a task still to do; the clue is tomorrow (future). ✗ bringing — remember + -ing means having a memory of something already done; ✗ bring — a bare infinitive cannot follow remember; ✗ brought — a past form has no auxiliary here and the action is in the future.

items.q: It rained all day on Saturday; ______, the school picnic was put off until next week.
items.vi: Thứ Bảy trời mưa cả ngày; do đó, buổi dã ngoại của trường bị hoãn sang tuần sau.
items.explanation: The second clause is the result of the first (rain → picnic put off), so the linker is consequently. ✗ however — shows contrast, but there is none; ✗ whereas — a conjunction joining two contrasting facts, not a sentence adverb after a semicolon; ✗ otherwise — means 'if not', which would say the picnic was put off because it did NOT rain.

items.q: If it ______ tomorrow, we will have PE in the gym instead of on the field.
items.vi: Nếu ngày mai trời mưa, chúng tôi sẽ học thể dục trong nhà thi đấu thay vì ngoài sân.
items.explanation: A real future possibility is the first conditional: if + present simple, will in the main clause (we will have PE). ✗ will rain — will never goes in the if-clause; ✗ rained — past simple makes a second (unreal) conditional, which needs 'would', not 'will', in the main clause; ✗ would rain — would does not go in an if-clause.

items.q: The final exam results ______ on the school website next Friday.
items.vi: Kết quả kỳ thi cuối kỳ sẽ được công bố trên trang web của trường vào thứ Sáu tới.
items.explanation: The subject results cannot announce anything — they are announced by the school — so the verb is passive, and next Friday makes it future: will be announced. ✗ will announce — active, so the results would be doing the announcing; ✗ are announcing — active, and present continuous for a fixed future date is odd; ✗ have announced — active and present perfect, but the announcement is still to come.

items.q: Lan said that she ______ a doctor when she grew up.
items.vi: Lan nói rằng khi lớn lên cô ấy sẽ trở thành bác sĩ.
items.explanation: After a past reporting verb (said) tenses shift back: will → would; the clause when she grew up is already in the shifted past form. ✗ will be — no backshift after said; ✗ is — present tense clashes with said and with 'when she grew up'; ✗ has been — present perfect says she has already been a doctor, which contradicts a childhood ambition.

items.q: Our maths teacher is strict, but she is always patient ______ slow learners.
items.vi: Cô giáo toán của chúng tôi nghiêm khắc, nhưng cô luôn kiên nhẫn với những học sinh tiếp thu chậm.
items.explanation: The adjective patient takes with before the person you are patient towards: patient with slow learners. ✗ to — follows kind/rude/polite (kind to), not patient; ✗ for — 'patient for' is not a phrase (you wait patiently for something); ✗ at — follows good/bad/clever (good at maths), not patient.

items.q: This winter is much ______ than last winter — I have to wear two jumpers to school.
items.vi: Mùa đông năm nay lạnh hơn nhiều so với mùa đông năm ngoái — tôi phải mặc hai cái áo len đi học.
items.explanation: Than signals a comparison of two winters, so a comparative is needed: much colder. ✗ cold — the base form cannot be followed by than; ✗ coldest — a superlative compares three or more and needs 'the'; ✗ the coldest — a superlative, and superlatives never take than.

items.q: Whenever I show my brother an essay, he ______ it and tells me everything that is wrong.
items.vi: Mỗi lần tôi đưa anh trai xem bài luận, anh ấy lại bới lông tìm vết và chỉ ra mọi lỗi sai.
items.explanation: Pick holes in = find faults in; the clue is tells me everything that is wrong. ✗ turns a blind eye to — deliberately ignores, the opposite of criticising; ✗ makes light of — treats as unimportant; ✗ pulls strings for — uses influence to help someone get something.

items.q: Lan: Do you ______ your new classmates? / Nam: Yes, they are really friendly.
items.vi: Lan: Cậu có hòa hợp với các bạn cùng lớp mới không? / Nam: Có, các bạn ấy rất thân thiện.
items.explanation: Get on with someone = have a friendly relationship; the reply they are really friendly confirms it. ✗ get over — recover from an illness or a shock; ✗ get away with — escape punishment for something; ✗ get through — finish or survive something difficult (an exam, a hard week).

items.q: I ______ my old primary school report while I was tidying my desk last night.
items.vi: Tối qua tôi tình cờ thấy học bạ tiểu học cũ của mình khi đang dọn bàn học.
items.explanation: A short action inside a longer one (while I was tidying) takes the past simple: came across. ✗ was coming across — the continuous is for the background action, and finding by chance is a sudden event, not a process; ✗ have come across — present perfect cannot go with the finished time last night; ✗ had come across — past perfect would put the finding BEFORE the tidying, but it happened during it.

items.q: Please check the new class ______ — chemistry has moved to Thursday afternoon.
items.vi: Hãy kiểm tra thời khóa biểu mới của lớp — môn hóa đã chuyển sang chiều thứ Năm.
items.explanation: A list of the times of school lessons is a timetable; the clue is chemistry has moved to Thursday afternoon. ✗ calendar — shows the days and months of the year, not lesson times; ✗ diary — a personal book of daily events or plans; ✗ menu — a list of dishes in a restaurant.

items.q: Keep the ______ in case the calculator stops working and you need to take it back to the shop.
items.vi: Hãy giữ hóa đơn phòng khi máy tính bỏ túi bị hỏng và bạn cần mang ra trả lại cửa hàng.
items.explanation: A receipt is the paper proving you paid — what a shop asks for when you take it back. ✗ recipe — instructions for cooking a dish (a common spelling mix-up); ✗ bill — a paper asking you to pay, given before payment; ✗ ticket — lets you travel or enter an event.

items.q: The weather ______ says it will be sunny and 32 degrees in Ho Chi Minh City tomorrow.
items.vi: Dự báo thời tiết nói ngày mai ở Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh trời nắng và 32 độ.
items.explanation: The fixed compound is weather forecast — a report of what the weather will probably be (says it will be sunny ... tomorrow). ✗ prediction — similar meaning, but not the noun that collocates with weather; ✗ estimate — a rough calculation of a number or cost; ✗ guess — an answer without evidence, not an official report.

items.q: To get a part-time job at the café, you have to fill in an ______ form first.
items.vi: Để xin làm thêm ở quán cà phê, trước tiên bạn phải điền vào đơn xin việc.
items.explanation: The form you fill in to ask for a job is an application form (clue: to get a part-time job). ✗ appointment — a fixed time for a meeting; ✗ advertisement — the notice announcing that a job is available; ✗ interview — the meeting that comes after you apply, not a form.

items.q: Nam wants to be a pilot, so he is ______ a lot of effort into his English lessons.
items.vi: Nam muốn trở thành phi công nên cậu ấy đang dồn rất nhiều công sức vào các tiết tiếng Anh.
items.explanation: The collocation is put effort into something (clue: into his English lessons). ✗ making — 'make an effort' exists, but it is followed by a to-infinitive, not into; ✗ taking — only a task 'takes effort' (it takes effort to ...); a person does not take effort into something; ✗ giving — 'give effort' is not an English collocation.

items.q: Lan: Can you come out and play? / Nam: Sorry, I haven't ______ my homework yet.
items.vi: Lan: Cậu ra ngoài chơi được không? / Nam: Xin lỗi, tớ chưa làm xong bài tập về nhà.
items.explanation: The verb that collocates with homework is do; with haven't ... yet (present perfect) it is done. ✗ made — make is for creating something new (make a cake, make a decision), never homework; ✗ taken — you take an exam or a test, not homework; ✗ given — a teacher gives homework; the student does it.

items.q: My uncle ______ as a chef in a hotel in Da Nang since 2019.
items.vi: Chú tôi đã làm đầu bếp ở một khách sạn tại Đà Nẵng từ năm 2019.
items.explanation: Since + starting point (since 2019) marks an action that began in the past and continues now: present perfect has worked. ✗ works — present simple describes a habit but cannot go with since + a date; ✗ is working — present continuous is a temporary action now, with no link back to 2019; ✗ worked — past simple means the job has finished, but since shows it still continues.
